leadIn:
I’m using the active settle workflow: I’ll inspect the renaming flow, tests, and repository history first, then bring only externally meaningful choices to the native question form before changing code.

This is a **bounded** change: the existing single-directory rename flow is in `src/rename.js`; no new subsystem or public data format is needed.

Verified facts:

- `applyRenames` executes sequential `renameSync` calls, so a later collision leaves earlier steps committed (`src/rename.js`, `applyRenames`).
- The CLI prints the entire plan before applying any rename (`src/cli.js`).
- Inputs are sorted filenames and numbering begins at `001` (`src/match.js`; `test/rename.test.js`).
- Accidental repeated runs are common, while undo/journaling is explicitly excluded (`README.md`, “How it is used” and “Out of scope”).

**Inference:** The core unresolved outcome is whether any invalid/colliding plan should prevent the whole batch or merely omit affected entries. That choice controls failure output, exit behavior, and repeated-run semantics; those decisions wait on it.

questions.question: When any planned target already exists, should the batch make no changes or continue around that entry? A wrong choice either preserves the current partial-run risk or silently produces an incomplete sequence. Evidence: `src/rename.js` currently stops after earlier renames, and `README.md` says accidental repeated runs are common.

options.label: Abort batch (Recommended)
options.description: Validate first and rename nothing on a collision; safest for scripted bulk runs, but one conflict blocks all otherwise valid renames.

options.label: Skip conflicts
options.description: Rename non-conflicting entries and report skipped ones; completes more work, but deliberately leaves a partial/incomplete batch.

leadIn:
The first decision settles known collisions as all-or-nothing, but three observable edges remain:

- `src/cli.js` currently writes every `from -> to` line before filesystem mutation, so a rejected plan would otherwise look as though it ran.
- `planRenames` can include a target that is also a matched source, and it can produce duplicate targets when the replacement has no `#` (`src/rename.js`).
- Planning and applying are separate calls with no lock; another process can change the directory between or during them (`src/cli.js`, `src/rename.js`).

**Inference:** We must define what counts as a blocking conflict, what stdout means on rejection, and how far the no-partial-work promise extends when the filesystem changes after validation. Tests and error handling wait on these answers.

questions.question: Should a target occupied by a file that this same plan will move count as a collision? The wrong choice either rejects safe rearrangements or requires cycle-safe execution. Evidence: `planRenames` may match existing numbered files because matching and target generation use the same directory (`src/rename.js`).

options.label: Allow planned moves (Recommended)
options.description: Treat destinations vacated by this batch as available and use safe staging; supports reruns/reordering, but adds temporary internal moves.

options.label: Reject any occupied
options.description: Abort whenever a different path already exists at planning time; simpler and conservative, but blocks rearrangements the batch could safely perform.

questions.question: What should stdout contain when validation rejects the batch? A wrong choice can mislead humans or break scripts parsing planned mappings. Evidence: `src/cli.js` currently prints the plan before applying it, while repository conventions reserve diagnostics for stderr.

options.label: No mappings (Recommended)
options.description: Keep stdout empty, explain the collision on stderr, and fail; unambiguous for scripts, but removes the current preview-like output on failure.

options.label: Print plan
options.description: Preserve all planned mappings on stdout and report rejection on stderr; useful for inspection, but mappings may be mistaken for completed work.

questions.question: If another process creates or changes a relevant file after validation while this run is applying, should this run roll back or stop where it is? The wrong choice determines whether the no-partial-work guarantee survives concurrent writers. Evidence: `src/cli.js` has no directory lock and `applyRenames` performs multiple filesystem operations.

options.label: Roll back (Recommended)
options.description: Attempt to restore this run’s completed moves and fail; strongest batch behavior, but rollback itself cannot be guaranteed under hostile concurrent changes.

options.label: Stop partial
options.description: Fail immediately and leave completed moves in place; simplest behavior, but retains the reported halfway state under races or I/O failures.

leadIn:
The chosen behavior now permits cycle-safe staging and requires rollback for failures discovered after work starts.

Repository closures now cover several remaining probes: an empty match already yields an empty successful plan (`planRenames`); repeat runs are expected (`README.md`); persistent journals/undo are excluded (`README.md`); and CLI failures already produce a nonzero process status through thrown filesystem errors (`src/cli.js`). No authorization model or external consumer exists beyond the local CLI.

Two user-visible failure details remain. **Inference:** reporting all validation defects makes one retry sufficient, while rollback residue reporting determines whether operators can safely recover from the rare case where restoration itself is obstructed. The exact diagnostics and corresponding tests wait on these answers.

questions.question: When preflight finds multiple conflicts, should stderr report all of them or only the first? A wrong choice changes how many inspect-and-retry cycles users need. Evidence: batches commonly contain 200–800 files (`README.md`), and validation will occur before stdout mappings are emitted.

options.label: Report all (Recommended)
options.description: List every conflicting or duplicate destination in one failure; easier recovery, but diagnostics can be long on a badly formed plan.

options.label: First only
options.description: Stop reporting after one conflict; concise, but users may need repeated runs to discover every problem.

questions.question: If a concurrent change prevents complete rollback, what should the diagnostic expose? A wrong choice can hide files left at temporary or target names. Evidence: no journal is allowed (`README.md`), so stderr is the only durable guidance from the failed invocation.

options.label: List leftovers (Recommended)
options.description: Report each path this run could not restore and leave no journal; actionable, but the error can include several pathnames.

options.label: Generic failure
options.description: Only say rollback was incomplete; shorter and less revealing, but forces manual directory inspection.

leadIn:
One last edge appears when replaying the full probe ledger:

- A replacement without `#` is accepted by the current parser and maps every source to the same destination (`src/rename.js`).
- Successful stdout currently describes intent before execution, not confirmed completion (`src/cli.js`).
- Your rollback choice means a late failure can occur after mappings would already have been printed.

**Inference:** Duplicate generated destinations must be explicitly classified, and stdout timing must have a single meaning across both preflight and late failures. These are the final unresolved contract points.

questions.question: If two sources generate the same target, should validation reject the batch or keep one source? A wrong choice either hides data loss/incompleteness or rejects ambiguous input. Evidence: `replacement.replace("#", ...)` leaves a replacement without `#` identical for every match (`src/rename.js`).

options.label: Reject batch (Recommended)
options.description: Report every duplicate target and change nothing; prevents ambiguity, but makes constant replacements invalid for multi-file matches.

options.label: Keep first
options.description: Rename only the first source and skip later duplicates; does some work, but silently produces an incomplete batch.

questions.question: Should mapping lines be emitted only after the whole batch succeeds, or as each move is attempted? A wrong choice affects whether scripts can treat stdout as a completion record. Evidence: `src/cli.js` currently emits all lines before `applyRenames`.

options.label: After success (Recommended)
options.description: Emit the full mapping only once the batch completes; stdout reliably means success, but long runs provide no progress stream.

options.label: During moves
options.description: Emit mappings as work progresses; gives live feedback, but failed runs leave stdout containing operations later rolled back.

leadIn:
The frontier is closed. User-settled ledger entries are:

- Collision outcome — “any pre-existing target?” → **abort the whole batch before changes**.
- Occupied target — “target is another planned source?” → **allow it with safe staging**.
- Rejected output — “stdout on preflight rejection?” → **no mappings**.
- Concurrent/late failure — “state after an apply-time failure?” → **attempt full rollback**.
- Validation diagnostics — “one or all conflicts?” → **report all**.
- Incomplete rollback — “what recovery detail?” → **list every unrestored path**.
- Duplicate destinations — “reject or keep one?” → **reject the batch**.
- Success output — “when emit mappings?” → **only after the whole batch succeeds**.

Resolved contract: preflight the complete plan; reject occupied external destinations and duplicate destinations with all diagnostics on stderr, nonzero exit, no stdout, and no filesystem changes. Destinations owned by sources in the same plan are valid and must work safely, including cycles/no-ops. Apply through temporary same-directory staging; on an unexpected failure, roll back completed work, report the original failure, and name any paths that could not be restored. Keep matching, numbering, single-directory scope, and the no-journal/no-undo policy unchanged.

The proof will be focused `node --test` cases for collision atomicity, duplicate rejection, planned-source rearrangement, repeat/no-op behavior, success-only stdout, rollback, and baseline numbering.

questions.question: Does this resolved contract capture the fix, exclusions, and proof correctly, or is anything materially missing or wrong?

options.label: Implement it (Recommended)
options.description: Proceed with this behavior and test contract; strongest atomicity available without adding the explicitly excluded persistent journal.

options.label: Revise contract
options.description: Pause implementation so you can correct a material outcome or exclusion; delays the fix but avoids encoding the wrong behavior.
